q: In the balance-transfer-propensity project, what do we know about feat-bt-util-trend-v2?
a: It is a six-month utilization slope plus the 3-month level from cards.accounts_monthly, clipped at +/-0.15 per month. Swapping it in for feat-bt-util-3m moved holdout AUC from 0.66 to 0.67; it is used in bt-xgb-v2 and bt-xgb-v3.

q: In the balance-transfer-propensity project, what came of exp-104-limit-headroom-full?
a: It showed that post-offer limit rows inflate random-split AUC from 0.74 to 0.81. That became find-bt-limit-leak, which led to dec-bt-drop-post-offer-features: all BT models drop limit rows dated after offer open.

q: In the balance-transfer-propensity project, what does bt-xgb-v2 use as inputs?
a: feat-bt-util-trend-v2, feat-bt-revolve-share, feat-bt-bureau-delta and feat-bt-limit-headroom (pre-offer rows only), trained on the ds-bt-offer-log exposures.

q: In the balance-transfer-propensity project, which model is the current BT mailer scorer?
a: bt-xgb-v3, in production since 2026-03-01. It uses the bt-xgb-v2 inputs but is trained on 12-month net margin per exposed account rather than acceptance, and it superseded bt-xgb-v2.

q: In the balance-transfer-propensity project, what AUC did bt-xgb-v2 reach on bt-holdout-2025q1?
a: 0.68 (n=41,800 held-out accounts, acceptance label), with KS 0.27 and top-30% lift 1.9x.

q: In the balance-transfer-propensity project, why was feat-bt-util-3m superseded?
a: A six-month utilization slope carries more signal than the 3-month mean and is more stable under limit changes. Swapping it in lifted holdout AUC from 0.66 to 0.67 (exp-103), and feat-bt-util-trend-v2 then went into bt-xgb-v2.
